title: the cast sweep and the casting-door probe read the artifact trail, not the index
intention: cast.py sweep_casts classifies each ticket by the first entry naming it in artifact.read_trail, and the_casting_door_has_callers counts from the trail; a ticket with no trail entry reads past_horizon, never unjournaled. The trail is per box and keeps 30 days; this reader sees only that, and says so.
traces_to: Law 3: a census that reads one entry per ticket reports a class it never measured. Law 7: an old ticket read as unjournaled is a false red in a record of truth.
how: Swap door.read_journal(commons_root) for door.read_trail(commons_root) in sweep_casts and in the probe. Add the class past_horizon for a ticket the index names but the trail does not. The docstrings and the probe's finding name the 30-day, per-box horizon. It builds after b15da5656579 lands, which adds read_trail and the index.

clauses.claim: a ticket written twice through a scratch world's door is classified by its first entry, read from the trail
a ticket the index names but the trail does not reads past_horizon, not unjournaled
the_casting_door_has_callers counts every trail entry in the horizon, and its finding names the 30-day horizon

why: Split from b15da5656579 under RULE 1. Akien, 16:47 UTC 2026-11-16, relayed verbatim by the orchestrator: "then how about this... the latest entry remains in cairn commons, and everything else broken into... per day? per week? inside of our .cairn/logs folder". After b15d the journal holds only the newest entry per path and every entry is in a day trail on this box for 30 days.

decisions.text: D1: the reader reads as the intention says.
D2: the red-first proof, one tooth per clause.

D3: test_cast_ticket's planted lines land where the door's land since b15da5656579, the index and the day trail; its probe world carries its own trail key, and its bin/cmd/cast --sweep run is handed the proof's world through CAIRN_ARTIFACT_ROOTS. The sweep counts gain past_horizon.
